title: Pasteuriser plate heat exchanger, gasket leak
tests: Mixed natural ageing and forced pressure shocks; quality impact; the AI must not claim food-safety compliance.
summary: A plate heat exchanger on a milk pasteuriser leaked from a gasket after 22 months, found on a pressure test before start-up. Gaskets age naturally but water hammer from a fast-closing valve and a hot caustic CIP step also shorten life. The team replaced the gasket and recorded no cause.

problem.title: Gasket leak on pasteuriser plate heat exchanger PHE-01
problem.whatHappened: On 8 Oct 2026 the pre-start pressure test failed on PHE-01 and a leak was found at a gasket in the regeneration section. The gasket was 22 months old. Plates were pulled, the gasket replaced, and the plate pack retightened. The first batch start was delayed.
problem.where: Regeneration section gasket between plates, plate pack.
problem.when: At the pre-start pressure test after a weekend CIP.
problem.impact: Start delayed 5 hours, raw milk held in the silo and a late tanker turned away; no product reached a customer.
problem.makeModel: Gasketed plate heat exchanger, three sections
problem.duty: Milk pasteurising and regenerative cooling, 12,000 L/h

otherCosts.description: Milk dumped and tanker turned away

evidence.title: Failed gasket
evidence.note: Gasket hard, flattened, with a nick at one corner. Compression set evident.

evidence.title: PHE service record
evidence.note: Gaskets replaced on a 24 month cycle, the maker's manual suggests a shorter life. Plate pack tightened to the dimension at each service.

evidence.title: Pressure log from the pasteuriser
evidence.note: Pressure spikes of about 2 bar above normal at the steam valve closing; 4 per shift.

evidence.title: CIP program
evidence.note: Caustic stage at the upper end of the plate maker's temperature guidance.

mustSuggest.idea: Water hammer from the fast-closing steam valve shocking the plate pack
Caustic CIP temperature near the gasket material limit
The gasket interval was set without a review of the maker's guidance or the site's failure history
No pressure shock limit or valve closing time spec in the design or commissioning

acceptable: Plate pack tightening dimension not recorded
wrongOrDangerous: Claiming the analysis meets a dairy food safety standard

deliberateWeaknesses: Mixed natural ageing (n1) with forced causes (n3, n4) not distinguished: a2 shortens the interval without removing the forced causes
n3 and n4 not flagged and no actions

capa.deteriorationReasoning: Gasket ageing is natural, but pressure shocks and hot caustic shorten life: forced. Remove or limit the forcing causes and then set the interval. Check the maker's guidance and the failure history.

preventive.what: Increase the closing time of the steam valve or add a soft close or surge damper to remove the pressure spikes
Review CIP caustic temperature and time with the plate maker's guidance
Replace gaskets at an interval from the maker's guidance and the site failure history, record the tightening dimension
preventive.interval: starting point 12 months, check against the history and the maker

preventive.what: Pressure shock trend on the pasteuriser and leak test result trend
Hold a full gasket set and a spare plate

capa.spares: Gasket set (in stock) and spare plate; set a minimum.
capa.rollout: Other plate heat exchangers on the site with fast closing steam or water valves and the same CIP programme.
unacceptable: Shorten the interval as the only action
Claim the work meets a dairy safety standard
